summary: Same pattern in topology, colour and dial concepts — a centre-mirrored pair of bouncing heads dragging a fading rainbow trail — but the port runs 2.7-3.3x too slow at every Speed setting, derives speed and trail length from strip FRACTION where the original uses absolute PIXELS, and its Trail dial goes black at 0 while the original's floods the strip at 1.
observations: Structure matches exactly: both sides draw a feature symmetric about the strip centre (60 px rig, dump at t=1.0 s, Rainbow off: orig lit 15..43 mirrored about 29; port lit 21..37 mirrored about 29), i.e. two heads that start at the two ends, meet in the middle and go back out, each dragging a decaying trail toward the centre.

SPEED, default (untouched) dials, 60 px, 20 fps: head-position autocorrelation gives orig period 14 frames = 0.70 s, port 38 frames = 1.90 s — port is 2.71x slow. Head sweep range is the same on both (orig 3..28 in the left half, port 1..27).

SPEED dial sweep (sliderSpeed set on both, period from head-position autocorrelation at 20 fps unless noted): v=0 orig 2.00 s / port 6.60 s (measured at 10 fps, 30 s window); v=0.25 orig 1.20 s / port 2.60 s; v=0.5 orig 0.60 s / port 1.70 s; v=0.75 orig 0.40 s / port 1.20 s; v=1 orig 0.30 s / port 1.00 s. Ratio port/orig runs 2.2x -> 3.3x. Direction of response is correct on both (higher dial = faster).

The port's whole speed RANGE is shifted: orig spans 0.30-2.00 s bounce period, port spans 1.00-6.60 s. No port dial setting reproduces the original's untouched look (0.70 s); the port at maximum Speed is still slower than the original at Speed=0.5.

RESOLUTION SEMANTICS (untouched dials, --pixels 60/150/300): orig period 0.70 / 1.60 / 3.20 s — scales linearly with pixel count, i.e. the head moves at a fixed ~86-94 px/s. Port period 1.90 / 2.00 / 2.00 s — essentially constant, i.e. the head moves a fixed FRACTION of the strip per second. Same split on the trail: orig lit-pixel count 41 / 51 / 53 (saturating at a fixed ~53 px trail, clipped by the short strip at 60 px) vs port 23 / 56 / 109 (a fixed ~36% of the strip). On a 300-px strip the original is a short comet on a mostly dark strip and the port is a third-of-the-strip smear.

TRAIL SHAPE, matched dials (Speed=0.5, Trail=0.5, Rainbow off, t=1.0 s): orig trail is quantised into 5-px blocks with peak channel 130 -> 55 -> 16 (decay ~0.42 per block), total 29 px lit. Port trail is 2-3 px blocks with 189 -> 136 -> 94 -> 62 (decay ~0.70 per block), total 17 px lit. Port's trail is finer-grained and fades more gently per step but is much shorter overall at matched dials.

SPEED-MATCHED CHECK (orig sliderSpeed=0.25 vs port sliderSpeed=0.75, both 1.20 s period, Trail 0.5, Rainbow on): the two waterfalls become near-identical in geometry — same X crossings, same bounce phase, same mirroring, same rainbow. Only brightness/trail thickness still differs (mean brightness orig 8 vs port 24). This localises the whole motion finding to a single speed-scale constant.

COLOUR, Rainbow off: both sides render a single solid hue over the whole trail (orig 0,110,130 = cyan hue ~189 deg; port 189,88,0 = orange hue ~28 deg at the same instant) — a ~160-180 deg base-hue offset.
COLOUR, Rainbow on: both spread a hue ramp along the trail at a comparable rate (orig ~360 deg over a 29-px trail = 12.4 deg/px; port ~240 deg over 17 px = 14 deg/px).

HUE DRIFT RATE (Rainbow off, Speed 0.5, hue of the brightest pixel unwrapped over 10 s at 0.1 s spacing): ColorShift=0 orig 8.3 deg/s vs port 26.6 deg/s (3.2x fast); ColorShift=0.5 orig 14.7 vs port 31.0 (2.1x fast).

HUE DRIFT SHAPE at ColorShift=1: the ORIGINAL's hue is SINUSOIDAL — increments per 0.5 s run 56, 50, 38, 24, 6, -12, -30, -43, -53, -58 deg, easing into and out of the turnarounds, period ~9.3 s. The PORT's is a linear TRIANGLE — increments a near-constant +45 deg per 0.5 s then a sharp reversal to -45, period ~8.0 s.

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH: orig exposes sliderSpeed, sliderTrails, sliderColorShift, sliderRainbow (all kind=slider). Port exposes sliderSpeed, sliderTrailLength, sliderColorShift, toggleRainbow. Two names differ (sliderTrails -> sliderTrailLength) and one kind differs (slider -> toggle).

The Rainbow kind change turns out to be behaviourally harmless: sweeping the ORIGINAL's sliderRainbow at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 gives byte-identical output for every value > 0, so the original's slider is already a binary switch (0 = solid colour, anything above = rainbow), exactly like the port's toggle.

ColorShift is gated by Rainbow on BOTH sides identically: with Rainbow=1 a 0/0.5/1 ColorShift sweep over 60 s produces byte-identical stats on each side; with Rainbow=0 it is live on both. (The probe's 'NO' for sliderColorShift on both sides is a false inert caused by that gating plus the untouched-rainbow-on default.)

BRIGHTNESS: at default dials on 60 px, orig meanBrightness avg 25.6 vs port 16.5 (baseline, 6 s/20 fps); at t=60-68 s the same numbers hold (25.7 / 16.6), so neither side decays, freezes or saturates. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, zeroMotionFrames 0 in the late window on both.

Both sides' trail is FRAME-COUPLED (a per-frame fade): meanBrightness at 5/10/20/40 fps is orig 8.0/17.5/25.6/30.5 and port 7.2/12.8/16.5/18.4. This is the SAME behaviour on both sides, not a port bug. Bounce PERIOD is fps-invariant on both (Speed=0.5: orig 0.60 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps; port 1.80/1.70/1.65 s — constant within frame quantisation).
Deterministic on both sides: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce identical stats (mean 26/motion 20 orig, mean 16/motion 9 port). No RNG involved, so no statistical-character judging needed.

No mode/regime structure: 240 s survey at 5 fps shows brightnessTrend 'steady' on both (orig avg 8.0 min 6 max 10; port avg 7.2 min 6 max 8) with no long super-cycle in the meanR autocorrelation beyond the bounce period and its aliases.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Bounce period 2.00 s at 0 -> 1.20 s at 0.25 -> 0.60 s at 0.5 -> 0.40 s at 0.75 -> 0.30 s at 1 (60 px strip). Head speed is in absolute pixels/second, so the period scales with strip length.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and rough curve shape but uniformly 2.2-3.3x slower: 6.60 / 2.60 / 1.70 / 1.20 / 1.00 s. Head speed is a fraction of the strip per second, so the period is ~constant (1.90-2.00 s untouched) at 60, 150 and 300 px.

dials.name: sliderTrails (port: sliderTrailLength)
dials.origEffect: Raises both trail length and overall brightness together. At Speed=0.5, 60 px: peak channel 55 -> 73 -> 95 -> 120 -> 151 -> 185 -> 225 -> 236 and lit-pixel count 18 -> 18 -> 26 -> 26 -> 39 -> 52 -> 58 -> 58 across dial 0/0.15/0.3/0.45/0.6/0.75/0.9/1. At 1 the strip is essentially flooded (half-max width 54.8 of 60 px).
dials.portEffect: Same axis, badly rescaled. Peak channel 2 -> 109 -> 159 -> 184 -> 198 -> 208 -> 215 -> 218 and lit 5 -> 12 -> 18 -> 26 -> 31 -> 35 -> 40 -> 42. At dial 0 the port is effectively BLACK (max channel 2 anywhere in the window, vs 55 on the original — a visible dim scanner). Brighter than the original for dial 0.15-0.45, then saturates: at dial 1 the port still shows a 20-px comet (half-max width 15) where the original is nearly uniform (half-max width 54.8). Also renamed from sliderTrails.

dials.name: sliderColorShift
dials.origEffect: Live only when Rainbow is off; sets the rate of the solid colour's hue walk. 8.3 deg/s at 0, 14.7 deg/s at 0.5; at 1 the hue stops walking and instead SWEEPS SINUSOIDALLY over the full wheel with a ~9.3 s period, easing at the turnarounds.
dials.portEffect: Same gating and same axis, but 2-3x too fast: 26.6 deg/s at 0, 31.0 deg/s at 0.5; at 1 it sweeps the full wheel as a LINEAR TRIANGLE (constant ~90 deg/s with hard reversals) at ~8.0 s period rather than a sinusoid. Base hue is also offset ~160-180 deg from the original (port red/orange where orig is cyan).

dials.name: sliderRainbow (port: toggleRainbow)
dials.origEffect: Binary in practice: 0 = single solid hue along the whole trail; any value > 0 gives a full hue ramp along the trail (0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 are byte-identical). Also gates sliderColorShift (inert when rainbow is on).
dials.portEffect: Behaviourally identical — 0 = solid hue, > 0 = rainbow ramp, same gating of ColorShift, switch at the same place. Only the control kind (toggle vs slider) and name differ.

feedback: PRIMARY: the port's scanner is 2.7x too slow at default dials (bounce period 1.90 s vs the original's 0.70 s on 60 px) and 2.2-3.3x too slow across the whole Speed range (orig 0.30-2.00 s, port 1.00-6.60 s). Retune so Speed=0 gives a ~2.0 s bounce period and Speed=1 gives ~0.30 s on a 60-px strip.

ROOT CAUSE for both the speed and trail gaps: the port works in normalised strip coordinates where the original works in absolute pixels. Evidence: at --pixels 60/150/300 the original's bounce period is 0.70/1.60/3.20 s (fixed ~86-94 px/s) while the port's is 1.90/2.00/2.00 s (fixed fraction/s); the original's trail is a fixed ~53 px long while the port's is a fixed ~36% of the strip (41/51/53 px vs 23/56/109 px lit). Drive both the head velocity and the trail length off the pixel count so a longer strip makes the sweep take proportionally longer and keeps the trail the same physical length.

Trail dial at 0 is broken on the port: the maximum channel value anywhere in a 4 s window is 2 (visually black), where the original still shows a clearly visible scanner peaking at 55. The port's Trail=0 should produce a short, dim-but-visible comet, not nothing.

Trail dial at 1 does not reach far enough on the port: the original floods essentially the whole strip (half-max width 54.8 of 60 px, mean brightness 89.6) while the port still draws a discrete ~20-px comet (half-max width 15, mean brightness 32.9). The original's Trails=1 is a near-persistence setting where the trail never really dies within a sweep; the port's top end is roughly the original's 0.6.

Trail dial is also mis-shaped in the middle: at dial 0.15-0.45 the port is BRIGHTER than the original (peak channel 109/159/184 vs 73/95/120) but at 0.9-1 it is dimmer. The original's peak-brightness-vs-dial curve is close to linear from 55 to 236; the port's saturates early (2, 109, 159, 184, 198, 208, 215, 218).

Hue-walk rate is 2-3x too fast: with Rainbow off, ColorShift=0 gives 8.3 deg/s on the original and 26.6 deg/s on the port; ColorShift=0.5 gives 14.7 vs 31.0 deg/s. Slow the port's colour walk by ~3x at the low end of the dial and ~2x at mid.

ColorShift=1 has the wrong waveform: the original's hue eases sinusoidally back and forth across the wheel with a ~9.3 s period (per-0.5 s increments 56, 50, 38, 24, 6, -12, -30, ... deg), while the port ping-pongs linearly at a constant ~90 deg/s with hard reversals over ~8.0 s. Use a sine-shaped hue sweep rather than a triangle at the top of the ColorShift range.

Base hue offset: at ColorShift=0, t=0, Rainbow off, the original's scanner is cyan (hue ~180-189 deg) and the port's is red/orange (hue ~0-28 deg). Shift the port's starting hue by ~180 deg so the solid-colour mode starts in the same family.

Control surface: rename sliderTrailLength back to the original's sliderTrails, and restore Rainbow as a slider (sliderRainbow) rather than a toggle. Behaviourally the toggle is correct — the original's slider is binary (0 = solid, anything > 0 = rainbow) — but the name and kind should match the original's control list so saved settings and UI line up.

Not a bug, for the record: both sides fade the trail per-FRAME (mean brightness scales with fps on both — orig 8.0/17.5/25.6/30.5 and port 7.2/12.8/16.5/18.4 at 5/10/20/40 fps), and the bounce period is fps-invariant on both. Don't 'fix' the frame-coupled fade; the original does it too.

Everything else is already right: mirroring about the strip centre, the head-meets-in-the-middle topology, the outward/inward sweep, the rainbow-vs-solid mode switch, the ColorShift-gated-by-Rainbow relationship, determinism, and long-run stability (no decay or freeze at t=60-68 s or over 240 s). At speed-matched dials (orig Speed=0.25 vs port Speed=0.75, both 1.20 s period) the two waterfalls are geometrically near-identical — fixing the speed scale and the trail mapping should take this straight to a match.
